Judgment calls: (a) OFF-FRAME COMPONENT - Resistor 5 has bbox centre (208.2,-52.2), above the top edge, so it is not drawn in the image. A pixel scan of all four frame borders finds exactly two wires leaving the frame, both at the top: x=110-111 (top of the left rail) and x=276-277 (top of the middle rail); no wire leaves the left, right or bottom edge (the three bottom-edge marks at x=190-192 and x=273-275/287-289 are the left-rail overshoot and the two long capacitor plates, not wires). Resistor 5's bbox spans x 167-250, i.e. horizontally between those two stubs, so it is inferred to bridge them off-frame. (b) The 4-way crossing at (284,36) (top horizontal vs middle rail) is read as a CROSSOVER, no connection, even though the pen left a small blob there. Reason: if it were a junction the middle-rail top stub would be the same node as the left-rail top stub, and off-frame Resistor 5 would be a dead short across a plain wire - a pointless element. Reading it as a crossover makes Resistor 5 series with the 5k Resistor 2 and gives a well-posed circuit with no redundant or dangling element, so per the protocol's 'prefer the reading that makes the circuit function' rule it is a crossover. THIS IS THE ONE CALL A HUMAN SHOULD RE-CHECK. (c) The 4-way crossing at (319,294) (20V horizontal vs middle rail) IS a junction: if it were a crossover, the 20V source and the 5A source would form an isolated two-source loop and the R-L-C loop would have no source at all. (d) The 4-way at (152,309) (GND lead / 20V branch vs left rail) IS a junction: if it were a crossover, net '0' would consist of only GND 3 and one source lead, leaving the 20V source with no return path. (e) DUPLICATE ANNOTATION: components 6 (V-DC) and 7 (I-DC) have essentially identical bboxes, (252.2,297.0) and (251.9,297.0). Zooming that region at 7x shows exactly ONE drawn symbol - a circle containing a rotated '-' and '+', i.e. the 20V DC voltage source - and every other listed component maps to a distinct drawn symbol (5k resistor, 5A source, 5mH inductor, capacitor, GND) plus the off-frame resistor. So id 7 is a duplicate/mis-class of the same circle. Per the 'never delete a component' rule both are KEPT and given the same two nets (the nodes the single symbol sits between); a human should decide whether to drop id 7. (f) V-DC 6 polarity read at 7x: the '-' bar faces the left rail, the '+' faces the middle rail, so index 0 = 0 (negative) and index 1 = n2; same index convention used for the duplicate id 7.
